analysis.title: US Growth Intact, Antipodeans Busy Calendar, And BRL Positioning Update
key_insights: US durable goods trendline remains strong, with recent months showing signs of acceleration.
Conference Board consumer confidence, present situation and expectations series all sit below the 5th percentile on a 5-year lookback.
Current financial conditions still point to being accommodative to nominal growth, per the FCI model.
Australia September CPI is due tonight. Average monthly headline expected at +63bps and median trimmed at +27bps.
A hotter-than-expected Australian CPI print is not a prerequisite for AUD strength. Stabilization in equity markets and risk sentiment can offset as a valuation driver.
AI winners, semiconductor trade and speculative growth baskets have recovered from recent max drawdown lows, supporting risk-on and higher-beta currencies.
The desk's FX Divergence publication made the case for AUD longs as a technical bounce, to be held into this week given the macro catalysts.
A 25bps RBNZ hike is broadly expected in New Zealand.
Hedge funds cut BRL longs sharply yesterday at a -5σ pace per the FX Flow Monitor.
Yesterday's USDBRL move was the largest daily loss in the past ten years. Spillover to broad EMFX has been limited so far.
The desk reflags upside risk for USDZAR on reduced carry appeal, downside risk to FY27 inflation and pressure from lower gold prices.
Largest daily movers adjusted for 3-month realized vol: broad EUR weakness, most acute in EURNZD (-2σ). G10 yields all within +/-1σ. USDTWD -1.3σ in EMFX.
